name: Marketing Machine
lede: Four missions, about ten minutes each. Each one is a small project from a normal marketing week: research, content, ad testing, and reporting. You do the work first, then find out why it held up.
description: Level 3 of an interactive AI course for marketers: research, content, ad testing, and reporting, each as a short hands-on project.

missions.name: Research Sprint
missions.hook: An AI research summary reads well and sounds sure. Your job is sorting what you can use today from what needs a check and what gets cut.
missions.objective: Sort an AI research summary into what to use, what to check first, and what to cut.

missions.name: Content Engine
missions.hook: From search intent to a published post, six steps. Decide who does each one, you, the AI, or both, and see how your pipeline scores.
missions.objective: Decide which steps of a content workflow belong to you, to the AI, or to both.

missions.name: Ad Copy Lab
missions.hook: AI will write you twenty ad variants before lunch. Testing them honestly is the hard part. Start by running two identical ads and watching one win.
missions.objective: Tell a real winner from luck, and design an ad test you can trust.

missions.name: Read the Numbers
missions.hook: Ask better questions of a weekly table, catch the shaky claims in an AI summary, then build the report prompt you can reuse every Monday.
missions.objective: Ask better questions of your data and spot the weak claims in an AI summary.

recap: Sort AI research into use, check, and cut. Ask it what it is unsure of.
Give AI the drafting. Keep intent, facts, voice, and the publish button.
Small numbers are noisy. Change one thing, wait, then decide.
Ask what moved, flag the claims the data cannot back, and reuse your report prompt.
next: Next up: Level 4, Build Mode. Turn your best prompts into repeatable workflows.
